design:
Decided with the operator on 2026-10-31:
- **The readable id is added beside the stored id, not in place of it.** `Task.id` is the primary key, 12 foreign keys and 7 plain columns hold it (`db/models.py`), and branch and checkout names validate it as `task-` plus lowercase hex (`worktrees.py:84`, `:191`). Rewriting all that on live data is expensive to undo and shows the operator nothing more. A readable id is resolved to the stored id once, where a request enters; the 61 internal `session.get(Task, ...)` calls keep working on stored ids.
- **Readable ids are unique per project; stored ids stay globally unique.** Two projects can each have BPS-3, so a readable id resolves only inside a project. Agent doors know their project from the run credential; operator routes carry it in the path.
- **The number comes from a high-water mark, never reused**, the rule `FR-n` follows (`spec_identity.py:74-96`). Unlike `FR-n`, parallel task creation is normal in a flow, so the database enforces uniqueness and minting holds under concurrency.
- **The Hub derives the acronym; the operator can edit it until the spec's first task exists.** After that it is fixed, because ids never change.
- **Branches and checkouts keep the hex id; commit messages name both.** Branch code reads the id back out of the name (`worktrees.py:1651`, `:2129`, `:2237`), and two projects may share a readable id.
- **A task with no spec keeps its project-acronym id when later linked to a spec.** The id never changes, and the card already shows the spec.
- **Existing tasks are numbered in creation order by the migration.**

**Hazard (Tier 2).** The migration runs on the operator's real data at their next restart after merging. It only adds new columns and values, and no stored id, branch or reference changes. Rollback is the migration's downgrade, which drops what it added; ids written in text after the upgrade would stop resolving, which is why the hex id stays visible in the drawer. The migration is exercised on a copy of the real database before the task is finished.

checked: utils.py:24, api/v1/tasks.py:916, spec_tasks.py:411: how ids are minted
db/models.py:745: single-column global primary key; 12 foreign keys and 7 plain columns hold it
worktrees.py:84,191-228,1651,2129,2237: branch and checkout names require task- plus lowercase hex, and are read back
61 session.get(Task, ...) calls across 21 hub modules: internal lookups stay on stored ids
schemas/tasks.py:18,21: the create route accepts caller ids that look readable
runner_events.py:71: the redactor's sk- alternative is case-sensitive at a word start
spec_identity.py:74-96: FR-n's high-water precedent, with no lock in spec_service.py
A survey found no regex parsing task ids out of free text; the UI has startsWith('task-') tests (EvidenceBrowser.tsx:38, SpecWorkspace.tsx:160)
limits: Nothing is driven yet; the drive task establishes the failing baseline
The migration's run time on real data is unmeasured until the hub task runs it on a copy
The criteria are proposed coverage, not passing tests

open_questions.question: Do existing tasks get readable ids? Answer: yes, in creation order (operator, 2026-10-31).
Who picks the acronym? Answer: the Hub derives it; editable until the spec's first task exists (operator, 2026-10-31).
Do branches and checkouts use the readable id? Answer: no; they keep the hex id, and commit messages name both (operator, 2026-10-31).
Does a task with no spec keep its id when linked to one? Answer: yes (operator, 2026-10-31).

problem: A task is named `task-5a9efc6d2670` everywhere: 12 random hex characters (`hub/hub/utils.py:24`, minted at `api/v1/tasks.py:916` and `spec_tasks.py:411`). Agents write that in messages and notes, the drawer shows it in full (`TaskDetailDrawer.tsx:530`), and the board card does not show it at all. Nobody can remember it, say it, or tell from it which spec a task belongs to, so following an agent's message to the board means copying and searching.

requirements.statement: Every task created through any door receives a readable id of the form ACRONYM-N: its spec's acronym if it belongs to a spec at creation, otherwise the project's acronym.

requirements.rationale: A deleted task's id still appears in old messages and notes; reusing it would point them at the wrong work.
requirements.statement: A readable id is unique within its project, including under simultaneous creation, and its number is never used again within that acronym, even after the task is deleted.
A task's readable id does not change when its spec is renamed or archived, when it is reassigned, or when a task with no spec is later linked to a spec.
An acronym of 2 to 5 uppercase letters and digits starting with a letter is derived from the title or name, and is unique within the project across specs and the project itself.

requirements.rationale: task-12 would be read as a stored id (`worktrees.py:84`), and a lowercase sk-12 is destroyed by the secret redactor (`runner_events.py:71`), which already cost every task id its name once (F118).
requirements.statement: An acronym can never be TASK or SK, in any case, whether derived or edited.

The operator can see a spec's acronym on its page and change it until the spec's first task exists; after that a change is refused, naming why. An edited acronym obeys the same shape, uniqueness and refusal rules.
Every operator route and agent tool that takes a task id, including prerequisites, accepts the readable id in any case as well as the stored id, and acts on the same task within the caller's project.
A stored task-hex id keeps resolving wherever it did, indefinitely, and branch and checkout names stay as they are.

requirements.rationale: The create route accepts caller ids such as BPS-3 today (`schemas/tasks.py:18`), and one could shadow a real readable id.
requirements.statement: A caller-supplied task id shaped like a readable id is refused at creation.

The readable id is what the board card, task drawer, prerequisite lists, build record, messages and agent turn prompts show to name a task, the drawer also shows the stored id, and the board search finds a task by either.
A commit message the Hub writes that names a task names both its readable id and its stored id.

After the migration, every existing task holds a readable id numbered in creation order within its acronym, and nothing else about it has changed. A task whose spec no longer exists takes the project's acronym.
On the trial Hub, a real agent turn names a task by its readable id, the operator finds it on the board by that id, every task tool accepts it, and the id is unchanged after the spec is renamed.

in_scope: A readable id for every new and existing task
An acronym per spec and per project, editable for a spec until its first task exists
The readable id shown wherever a task is named to the operator or an agent
Every task route and tool accepting the readable id as well as the stored id
A migration on live data, with its rollback named
non_goals: Changing the primary key or the columns that reference it
Rewriting ids already written in old messages, notes or commits
A recommended builder and checker per task (slice recommended-people)
Redesigning the Build dialog or the spec header
Readable ids for runs, messages, documents or other records
Finding a task by readable id across projects
Editing a project's acronym or an acronym already in use

summary: Every task, old and new, gets a short id made of its spec's acronym and a number, such as BPS-3, or the project's acronym when it has no spec. The id is shown wherever a task is named and accepted wherever a task id is, and never changes.
